newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Pibor vols stay high as polls toss market.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Pibor vols stay high as polls toss market.

text.p: Implied volatility of options on Pibor futures remained sky-high on Friday as opinion polls continued to rock the underlying futures market, traders said.
"The market is very reactive to the various polls that are coming out suggesting various results in the parliamentary elections," said one broker at a French house in London.

Brokers said talk swirled through French markets on Friday that a poll by BVA appearing in Paris Match next week would show a mixture of the Socialists and Communits marginally ahead in the election race. A spokesman from BVA said the poll would begin Friday and it would not have any final results until Monday.
Another was due from IFOP in the Sunday newspaper Journal du Dimanche. Dimanche said it was under the impression the poll was still being conducted.
"It has had a big influence," said a trader at a French brokerage in Paris of the poll rumours.
On Thursday, an IPSOS poll for the weekly Le Point showed the governing centre-right ahead by only a thin margin in the election set for May 25-June 1.
The broker in Paris quoted implied volatility of June Pibor options at 36.0/40.0 percent, September at 26.0/28.0 percent, and December at 21.0/22.5 percent, broadly unchanged from Thursday.
Only ten days ago, before the election was called, June Pibor option volatility was at 20 percent, he said.
June Pibor futrues were quoted at 96.28 at 1401 GMT, down six basis points from Thursday and well off a high of 96.69 last Thursday when rumours of an election began.

The broker in London said the real problem for the market was that some Socialists have indicated they would seek talks to review the convergence criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Socialist leader Lionel Jospin has been sceptical about the criteria and Elizabeth Guigou, a Socialist Euro-MP who was France's negotiator leading up to the Maastricht Treaty said on Thursday a French Socialist government would seek talks.
The tader in London said non-resident investors were busy in Pibor options.
Among active trade, one house executed a put spread, buying 2,000 lots of 96.20 puts and selling 2,000 lots of 95.80 puts.
